title: In 1908, an Explosion Flattened 80 Million Trees in Siberia

scenes.text: In 1908, an explosion flattened 80 million trees in Siberia.
Eight hundred square miles of forest, flat in one morning. No crater.
The blast was about 250 times Hiroshima. Windows shattered hundreds of miles away.
Witnesses saw a fireball brighter than the Sun, then a shockwave that knocked people off their feet.
Nobody went to look for 19 years. The trees still lay flat, all pointing away from one spot.
A space rock around 200 feet wide, exploding in mid air. It never touched the ground.

description:
On June 30, 1908, an explosion over the Tunguska River in Siberia flattened an estimated 80 million trees across more than 800 square miles.
The blast released around 4 to 5 megatons, hundreds of times the Hiroshima bomb, yet left no crater: a stony asteroid roughly 50 to 80 metres wide exploded several miles up. The first scientific expedition didn't reach the site until 1927 and found the trees still lying flat, pointing away from the centre.
What would you do if you saw a fireball brighter than the Sun? Comment below.
first_comment: Some scientists have pointed out that had it arrived a few hours later, Earth's rotation would have put it over Europe instead of empty forest. Do you think we'd spot one like it coming today?
